elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "The Issuer may terminate this Agreement, and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement, for convenience and without cause..." The Issuer is the customer-side party (the Servicer/Cellco is the counterparty). There are no Order Forms in this servicing structure, so agreement-level termination is the full scope available.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "...upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly the preferred 30-day written notice, no additional conditions or consents attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "...and the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination." The word "pro rata" is express (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), the payer is the Vendor-side Servicer, and the trigger is the new convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1 No Resignation: "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." Resignation is barred except on legal inability, which is not a convenience right; the only other exit is Indenture Trustee removal for a continuing Servicer Termination Event (Section 7.2(c)), i.e. for cause. Correctly left untouched.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (and more Customer-favourable). Fallback level therefore is not complete on its own terms, but the preferred level is.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the inserted clause imposes no early-termination fee, penalty or make-whole, and no retained provision charges one on an Issuer-initiated exit, so the three-month cap is satisfied vacuously.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 7.1 gives the Servicer no convenience/resignation right at all (only legal inability), which is strictly better than an end-of-term-only right. Note the drafter was right not to import the fallback here — doing so would have granted the Servicer an end-of-term convenience exit it does not currently have.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no Servicer convenience termination right in existence under Section 7.1, there is no convenience notice period to lengthen.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single inserted sentence supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the express pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees, while retained Section 7.1 already denies the Servicer any convenience exit.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" reflects the ORIGINAL text (and a literal search for the alias "Customer"); the operative party here is the defined "Issuer". Inspected in substance, the rendered redline plainly contains an unconditional Issuer election to terminate for convenience, so the finding of deviation on the original and completeness of the redline both stand.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no survival tail, expense, procedure or damages language is added, and the drafter correctly dropped the model clause's "in whole or in part" (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists here). The added phrase "and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement" tracks the existing Section 7.2(c) removal formula so the new termination feeds the Section 7.4 Successor Servicer machinery, so it is functional rather than cosmetic.

Intent is preserved: the for-cause removal mechanics in Section 7.2(c)-(d), the Section 7.1 resignation bar, and the Section 8.3 natural termination trigger all survive without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Housekeeping only (not an element defect): the insertion is rendered without a section number. Number it (e.g. Section 7.3) or state where it sits so later cross-references to Article VII remain clean.

Optional confirmation, not required for completeness: verify that Section 7.4 conditions effectiveness of any termination on appointment of a Successor Servicer; if it does, the 30-day notice will operate subject to that, which is consistent with the retained structure and should be flagged to the client rather than redlined.
Fallback is not independently complete because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90; this is more favourable to us and is irrelevant given the preferred level is met.
